authoredSolutions.164: For differentiability on \(R\), \(f\) must be continuous and have matching derivatives at \(x=1\). Continuity: \(1+3+a = b+2 \Rightarrow b = a+2\). Left derivative \(f'(x)=2x+3\) gives \(5\) at \(x=1\); right derivative is \(b\), so \(b=5\) and \(a=3\). Thus \(f(x)=x^{2}+3x+3\) for \(x\le 1\) and \(5x+2\) for \(x>1\). Then \(\int_{-2}^{2}f\,dx=\int_{-2}^{1}(x^{2}+3x+3)\,dx+\int_{1}^{2}(5x+2)\,dx=\frac{15}{2}+\frac{19}{2}=17\).
authoredSolutions.168: For the \(\log\) term need \(\frac{2x+3}{4x^{2}+x-3}>0\). Since \(4x^{2}+x-3=(4x-3)(x+1)\), a sign chart gives \(x\in\left(-\frac{3}{2},-1\right)\cup\left(\frac{3}{4},\infty\right)\). For \(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x-1}{x+2}\right)\) need \(-1\le\frac{2x-1}{x+2}\le 1\), i.e. \(\frac{x-3}{x+2}\le 0\) and \(\frac{3x+1}{x+2}\ge 0\), giving \(x\in\left[-\frac{1}{3},3\right]\). The intersection is \(\left(\frac{3}{4},3\right]=(\alpha,\beta]\), so \(\alpha=\frac{3}{4},\ \beta=3\) and \(5\beta-4\alpha=15-3=12\).
